markdown_report:
The best first step remains a **controlled final-position rank probe**, strengthened with alignment checks, shortcut controls, and a prespecified decision rule. It tests training fit and candidate confusability; no diagnostic results or validation improvements are available yet.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training margins depend on score scale and sampled negatives. Fixed-candidate ranks improve comparability but remain sensitive to candidate construction. (2) Existing probes aggregate sequence positions. Final-position diagnostics better match inference, provided shifted targets and left padding are handled correctly. (3) Feedback identifies weak adjacent-interest recommendations and insufficient recent-interest specificity. These motivate challenges without establishing compatibility, satisfied ownership needs, or causal preferences.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Sampling research [1,2,5] shows that candidate selection can change model comparisons. Freeze diagnostic distributions and distinguish sampled sensitivity from full-catalog quality. (2) History-edit research [3] motivates controlled sensitivity tests. Equal-count deletions reveal dependence, without identifying causal intent. (3) The TREC rubric [4] separates unknown compatibility from incompatibility. Missing evidence must remain unknown. (4) Evaluation guidance [6,7] supports paired comparisons while warning that adaptive selection compromises confirmatory interpretation. User bootstrapping cannot estimate training-seed uncertainty.

These insights define three research directions: ranking discrimination, history dependence, and evidence sufficiency.

| Direction | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discrimination | Training score margins | Frozen final-position rank challenges and shortcut controls | Memorization and relationship to validation gains |
| Dependence | History edits [3] | Equal-count random, oldest, and newest deletion controls | Positional effects and causal interpretation |
| Evidence | Compatibility rubric [4] | Source-linked labels with abstention | Sparse attributes and annotation reliability |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Controlled rank probe — 4/7/5.** Originality: useful task-specific integration; established components. Potential: reusable across architectures; decision value remains untested. Difficulty: existing hooks help; alignment, matched pools, and reproducibility require care. Inspired by [1,2,5].
2. **Controlled history deletion — 5/7/5.** Originality: combines content groups with random controls; interventions already exist. Potential: tests interference hypotheses; deletion and position shifts confound interpretation. Difficulty: inference-only implementation; compaction and position-preserving masking require separate handling. Inspired by [3].
3. **Evidence-linked recommendation audit — 5/7/6.** Originality: connects feedback to source evidence; annotation frameworks exist. Potential: exposes unsupported assumptions; metadata may be insufficient. Difficulty: simple schema; evidence extraction and agreement assessment are demanding. Inspired by [4].

At 0% progress, select **idea 1** for feasibility and architecture compatibility. Its ratings are reduced for limited novelty and unproven usefulness, with higher implementation difficulty reflecting essential controls.

```text
freeze training records: target=h[t], prefix=left_pad(h[:t][-L:])
skip empty prefixes; preserve earlier occurrences of the target
freeze 99 unique distractors per challenge and eligible record:
    training-sampler, popularity-matched, text-similar
for each frozen checkpoint and record:
    features = log2feats(prefix)[:, -1, :]
    scores = predict_score(features, candidates)
    record target rank with deterministic tie-breaking
compare with popularity, shuffled-prefix, target-permutation controls
aggregate by dataset, challenge, target recurrence, and coverage
return metrics and explicit metric_definitions
```

Compute training-only item counts per dataset; publish positive-count deciles without splitting ties and a separate zero-count bin. Popularity matching samples uniformly within the target's bin; expand sparse pools by nearest log-count distance, breaking ties by item ID. Document the training sampler's actual distribution. Exclude padding, target, and observed prefix items from distractors; preserve legitimate earlier target occurrences in the prefix. Use identical eligible catalogs across challenges and report exclusions, expansions, and insufficient pools.

Freeze title-plus-description preprocessing, TF-IDF settings, vocabulary, IDF corpus, and L2 normalization. Separate similarity to the target from similarity to the latest history item. Resolve cosine ties by item ID; mark zero-vector text unavailable and report popularity-pool backfills. Compare semantic and random distractors using identical popularity-bin quotas, metadata coverage, and text-length strata; add a text-only baseline. Freeze multiple candidate draws using stable keys, recording IDs and common-record coverage. Semantic neighbors have unknown relevance: rank changes measure confusability, not demonstrated preference errors.

Assert shifted alignment, unique candidates, exactly one target, finite scores, batch dimensions, causal invariance, and candidate-permutation equivariance [8,9]. Repacked final-position measurements differ from loader-position measurements. Report absent measurements as unavailable; retain existing embedding and margin metrics with their scale and interpretation limitations.

Prespecify diagnostic-triggered ablations before observing validation outcomes—for example, stronger semantic confusability triggers one popularity-matched hard-negative training ablation, retaining uncertainty about false negatives. Compare its validation gain per total GPU-second with ordinary tuning under equal budgets. Frozen probes alone cannot establish better training decisions.

Preserve all adapter interfaces, four routes, DATA_DIR, seeds, predictor-writer consistency, and pinned macro validation HR@10. Charge diagnostics, training, debugging, and failures to 43,200 GPU-seconds. Report paired validation gains/losses and exploratory within-dataset user-bootstrap macro intervals; prespecify contrasts and use Holm correction if testing a family. Adaptive selection remains exploratory [7], and seed 42 supports only run-conditional conclusions. For twenty training users, keep full-catalog unseen-item coverage, popularity, concentration, and overlap descriptive; audit source evidence and unknown labels against explicit feedback without inferring unobserved traits.

idea.description: Add deterministic, correctly aligned final-position training-fit challenges to the compatibility-preserving diagnostic adapter. Compare frozen training-sampler, popularity-matched, and text-similar distractors, with shortcut controls and a prespecified connection to a limited training ablation.
idea.motivation: The existing margins mix positions and depend on score scale and negative selection. Controlled ranks can characterize adjacent-item confusability, but training memorization, popularity, text coverage, and positional alignment must be controlled before interpreting the results. The diagnostic's practical value must be measured through validation improvement per total search cost.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing embedding and margin probes, explaining that embedding alignment is not recommendation diversity and absolute margin thresholds depend on score scale. Use only public training histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; unavailable review fields, product categories, prices, ratings, and simulator traits must not be inferred.
Construct records by interaction index: target=h[t], prefix=h[:t], truncate to the latest L events, and left-pad to L. Skip empty prefixes. Earlier occurrences of the target are legitimate history; exclude the target event itself. For independently repacked prefixes, use features[:, -1, :]. For loader diagnostics, pair positive[b,j] with features[b,j,:] and sequence[b,:j+1]; never score an earlier target using the final complete-prefix representation. Record that repacking changes absolute positions.
Freeze checkpoint, record selection, candidate IDs, settings, and tie policy across comparisons. Use stable cryptographic seed derivation from seed 42, dataset, user, interaction index, challenge, and replicate rather than process-dependent hash(). Scope item IDs and all popularity statistics by dataset. Count training interactions per item; publish zero-count and tied positive-count decile boundaries. Sample popularity-matched negatives uniformly within the target bin, expanding by nearest log1p(count) distance with item-ID ties. Document the baseline training sampler distribution and exclusions; if it differs from the common diagnostic eligibility rule, label the diagnostic a conditioned sampler challenge rather than an exact reproduction.
Exclude padding, target, and observed prefix items from distractors, preserving target recurrence in the input. Draw 99 distinct distractors where feasible; skip and report insufficient pools instead of silently shrinking candidate sets. Save candidate IDs and pool expansion rates beneath the trial directory.
For semantic challenges, freeze title-plus-description normalization, tokenizer, vocabulary, IDF corpus, vectorizer parameters, and L2 normalization. Build the index from permitted catalog text without external weights. Report latest-history-item similarity and target similarity as separate challenges; the latter uses the known training diagnostic target solely to construct distractors. Rank cosine ties by item ID. Treat missing or zero-vector text as unavailable, documenting popularity-matched fallback rates. Compare semantic versus random candidates within identical popularity-bin quotas, metadata coverage, and prespecified text-length strata; use common records and multiple frozen draws. Unknown distractor relevance and possible false negatives limit preference-error interpretations.
For features [B,D], shared candidate IDs [C] require features @ embeddings.T; per-example IDs [B,C] require summed elementwise products with features[:,None,:]. Both return [B,C]. Adapt these operations to the actual architecture and compatibility hook. Check B=1 and C=1, compare vectorized scores against scalar scoring, and assert valid IDs, padding, exactly one target, unique negatives, finite scores, causal invariance where the architecture is causal, and candidate-permutation equivariance. Resolve score ties by ascending item ID.
Add training-count and prespecified timestamp-decayed popularity baselines, a text-only baseline, shuffled-prefix controls, and target permutations within dataset and popularity bin. Freeze the temporal reference and decay constant for timestamp popularity. Stratify novel versus repeated targets. Training-derived ranks remain measures of training fit, including freshly sampled records. High training ranks and weak validation indicate a fit/generalization gap.
Run view.model.eval() under no_grad and restore its prior mode, including when exceptions occur. Preserve measured values, counts, coverage, definitions, and unavailable states in the interpreter prompt. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Any inference architecture change must update the predictor writer for working/predict.py.
Before inspecting validation results, freeze a small contrast family and diagnostic-triggered decisions. For example, use a reproducible semantic-confusability gap to trigger one popularity-matched hard-negative mixture ablation, retaining the original loss and acknowledging false-negative risk. Compare against ordinary tuning with equal total GPU-second allocations; include diagnostic, retraining, debugging, and failed-run costs within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Select exclusively by the unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. If permitted per-user validation outputs exist, retain paired hit gains/losses, bootstrap paired users independently within categories, and average category differences equally. Exact McNemar tests can describe category-level discordance; apply Holm correction across prespecified tested contrasts. Post-selection intervals remain exploratory and do not account for adaptive search or training-seed uncertainty. Do not change the required training seed or access test labels for confirmation.
For the twenty training users, retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations and report coverage, popularity, concentration, and list overlap descriptively. Evidence audits should cite supporting history and exact permitted text, separate unknown compatibility from explicit mismatch, distinguish supported near-duplicates from topical similarity, and report label counts, agreement, and disagreements with explicit feedback by dataset. These observations do not establish population reliability or latent user traits.
idea.pseudocode:
records = freeze_indexed_training_records(seed=42, prefix_rule='left_pad(h[:t][-L:])')
assert_record_alignment_and_padding(records)
pools = freeze_training_counts_and_permitted_text_index(settings)
challenges = freeze_candidate_ids(records, pools, n_negatives=99, replicates=prespecified_replicates)
previous_mode = view.model.training
view.model.eval()
try:
    with torch.no_grad():
        run_alignment_scoring_and_invariance_checks(view)
        for batch in records:
            features = view.log2feats(batch.left_padded_prefixes)[:, -1, :]
            for challenge in challenges.for_batch(batch):
                scores = score_with_explicit_batch_shapes(view, features, challenge.item_ids)
                ranks = target_ranks(scores, challenge.item_ids, tie_break='item_id_ascending')
                accumulate(batch.dataset, challenge.type, batch.target_recurrence, ranks)
        run_frozen_popularity_text_shuffle_and_target_permutation_controls()
finally:
    view.model.train(previous_mode)
raw = {'metrics': aggregate_with_counts_coverage_and_unavailable_states(),
       'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions_and_limitations()}
# Keep original embedding/margin diagnostics alongside these measurements.
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw) embeds measurements and definitions,
# identifies training fit and confusability, and distinguishes hypotheses from evidence.
# Apply only prespecified diagnostic-triggered ablations.
# Select using unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10 and record total GPU cost.
return raw

originality.positive: Combines architecture-compatible final-position probes, matched distractors, shortcut controls, and a decision-cost assessment for the observed adjacent-interest failure.
originality.negative: Its ranking, sampling, text similarity, and intervention components are established; the contribution is primarily a controlled diagnostic protocol.

future_potential.positive: Could support reproducible architecture and loss comparisons while testing whether diagnostic guidance improves validation gains per search cost.
future_potential.negative: Training-fit diagnostics may fail to predict generalization, and their decision value has not been demonstrated.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing feature and scoring hooks and needs no external weights or initial retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct shifted alignment, batch scoring, matched candidate construction, controls, persistence, and cost accounting require substantial care.

related_work.title: [1] Sampling reliability research referenced in the supplied search results
contributions: Reports that sampling bias can change relative model rankings, motivating fixed diagnostic candidate sets.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed diagnostic predicts validation improvements.
Sampled rankings do not establish full-catalog recommendation quality.

related_work.title: [2] Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study referenced in the supplied search results
contributions: Examines interactions between negative-sampling methods and dataset popularity bias using repeated experiments and hyperparameter optimization.
limitations: Does not validate this four-category diagnostic protocol or its proposed training decisions.

related_work.title: [3] Scarcelli et al. (2025), interaction-history editing research
contributions: Searches for minimal interaction-history edits that change recommendations, motivating controlled sensitivity probes.
limitations: Recommendation changes after history edits do not identify causal user preferences.
Deletion can change sequence positions as well as content.

related_work.title: [4] TREC Product Recommendation 2025 annotation rubric
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes, related products, and complements, including compatible, unknown-compatibility, and incompatible cases.
limitations: Does not supply missing product attributes or validate automated annotations for the twenty training users.

related_work.title: [5] Krichene and Rendle, On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes limitations of sampled recommendation metrics, supporting explicit separation of candidate sensitivity from full-catalog performance.
limitations: Does not make a particular distractor distribution an unbiased proxy for full-catalog ranking.

related_work.title: [6] Offline evaluation guidance referenced in the supplied reflection results
contributions: Supports careful offline comparisons using user-level paired observations.
limitations: User-based uncertainty estimates do not capture training-seed variability or repair adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: [7] Adaptive holdout research
contributions: Explains why repeated adaptive use of held-out data can undermine ordinary generalization claims.
limitations: Prespecified contrasts and multiplicity correction alone do not remove bias from choosing checkpoints on the same validation users.

related_work.title: [8] Original SASRec shifted training sampler
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for shifted sequence inputs and next-item targets.
limitations: An implementation reference does not verify the local adapter's alignment or architecture-specific scoring.

related_work.title: [9] SASRec PyTorch model implementation
contributions: Illustrates final-position feature extraction and item-embedding scoring.
limitations: Scoring shapes and feature semantics must still be checked against the actual trained model.

related_work.title: Temporal popularity baseline study referenced in the supplied reflection results
contributions: Motivates explicit temporal definitions when constructing popularity baselines.
limitations: Does not determine the appropriate decay constant for these four datasets.

related_work.title: Multi-run evaluation study referenced in the supplied reflection results
contributions: Highlights uncertainty when drawing conclusions from few training runs.
limitations: Does not supply training-seed uncertainty for this required seed-42 experiment.

related_work.title: Scikit-learn pairwise metrics documentation
contributions: Documents cosine similarity used to compare normalized TF-IDF vectors.
limitations: Text similarity does not establish functional compatibility or user relevance.

related_work.title: Ihemelandu and Ekstrand, sampled evaluation research
contributions: Motivates controlling interactions between candidate sampling and popularity bias.
limitations: Matching popularity and metadata reduces measured confounding without guaranteeing equivalent relevance distributions.
